L263@P3: In an inner product space, the following identities
L264@P3: may be readily verified to hold for any pair of vectors

L266@P3: 4(j, g)= 11/+gjI2-II/-gI12 + i 11/+ ig 112 - i 11/- igW·
L267@P3: The first is known as the parall elogram law. The second is known as the polarization identity.
L268@P3: The parallelogram law suggests that the norm on a
L269@P3: Hilbert space is of a special kind. Obviously, not
L270@P3: every norm on a linear space satisfies this law, and
L271@P3: thus could not be obtained from an inner product.
L272@P3: An early result of P. Jordan and J. von Neumann states
L273@P3: that a Banach space (normed linear space for which
L274@P3: the resulting metric space is complete) is a Hilbert
L275@P3: space, that is, has a norm derivable from an inner
L276@P3: product, if and only if the norm satisfies the parallelogram law.
L277@P3: A basis {cpj} in .p is by definition a maximal orthonormal family of vectors; the index set J of subscripts
L278@P3: j is not necessarily countable. It is a consequence of
L279@P3: Zorn's lemma (which is equivalent to Zermelo's axiom
L280@P3: of choice) that in every Hilbert space there are bases.
L281@P3: The cardinal number of elements in any two bases
L282@P3: of the given space is always the same and defines
L283@P3: the dimension of the space. Any orthonormal family
L284@P3: of vectors in .p can be made part of a basis.
L285@P3: We mention in passing that every finite-dimensional
L286@P3: normed linear space generates a necessarily complete
L287@P3: metric space. Moreover, any two norms on the same
L288@P3: finite-dimensional linear space generate equivalent
L289@P3: topologies. More precisely: Any two normed linear
L290@P3: spaces of the same finite dimension (and over the same
L291@P3: scalar field) are necessarily linearly homeomorphic.
